traces.hint: Install a skill and watch where it lands and who can then use it.

steps.s: You open the Marketplace. The app asks the online store for the catalog.
The store sends back the list, with ratings and install counts.
You press Install. The app downloads the item to your computer.
The skill is copied into the folder Claude Code reads. Any hooks or tools it needs are registered.
YouCoded's own engine reads the same installed skills, so it can use it too.
The app tells the store what you installed. That is where install counts come from.
Your next chat, in any project, can use the skill.

traces.hint: Change something on one computer and watch it reach your other one.

steps.s: You change a file in a project. Sync notices a moment later.
Sync copies the change to your own GitHub account, into a hidden copy that never touches a repository of your own.
On your other computer, Sync hears about it (a live signal, or its regular check) and pulls the change down.
It writes the new file into that computer's copy of the project.
If both computers changed the same file at once, today you only get a short warning. Safer handling is still being built.
Your chat is a file; Sync notices it grew and picks it up.
Sync copies it to your own GitHub account, into a hidden copy that never touches a repository of your own.
On your other computer, Sync hears about it and pulls it down.
Before it opens there, sync checks no other computer is writing to this chat, then saves it into that computer's chat files.
You resume the chat. The keeper reads the file and the conversation is back on screen.
